chapters.title: US Dollar
chapters.teaser: The dollar index held near 102.2 in Asia after the Federal Reserve's hold on Wednesday. Markets trimmed their bets on a December Fed hike to about 78%. US growth and inflation figures at 7:30 AM CT are the first real test since the decision.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Since the US–Iran war began in February, high oil has kept US inflation near 3.7%, and the Federal Reserve raised rates in September. On Wednesday the Fed held its range at 3.75–4.00%, with two officials voting for an immediate hike, while chair Kevin Warsh refused to commit to December. What changed: Overnight the dollar index steadied near 102.2, just above Wednesday's post-decision low. Futures now price a December hike at about 78%, down from about 84% before the decision, as traders read Warsh as patient. Asian shares slipped after Google's owner Alphabet fell about 9% in late trading on results, but that did not send money into the dollar. What it means: The Fed's next move still looks like a hike, which keeps a floor under the dollar, but the timing now depends on the data rather than on a promise. That makes today's figures matter more than usual. The question to keep asking: does the next inflation reading make a December hike unavoidable?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: US third-quarter growth (forecast 3.0% annualized), the September PCE price index (core expected up 0.3% on the month, about 3.7% annualized, almost twice the Fed's 2% goal) and weekly jobless claims, all at 7:30 AM CT. The next Fed decision is December 9.
numbers: December Fed hike ~78% priced (CME via Reuters, from ~84% before the decision)
Core PCE forecast +0.3% m/m; Q3 growth forecast 3.0% annualized

scenarios.base: Growth and inflation land close to forecasts; December stays mostly priced and the dollar index holds between about 101.8 and 102.5.
scenarios.bull: Core PCE runs hotter than 0.3% on the month; December hike bets climb back toward 85–90%, short-term yields rise and the index pushes above 102.5.
scenarios.bear: Core PCE comes in at 0.2% or less, or growth disappoints; with Warsh already patient, December bets fall and the index slips toward 101.5.

chapters.title: Euro
chapters.teaser: The euro slipped to about $1.114 in Asia, giving back part of Wednesday's gain. The European Central Bank decides at 8:15 AM CT and is expected to hold; what it says about a December hike, and about France, matters more.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Energy costs from the Iran war have pushed euro-area inflation to about 3.8%, and the European Central Bank raised its deposit rate twice this year, to 2.50%. France's budget fight has kept a weight on the euro. What changed: Overnight the euro eased about 0.1% to near $1.114 as the dollar steadied. Markets see an October hold as almost certain and a December hike as likely, with roughly three more hikes priced over the next year. What it means: A hold is fully expected, so the euro's move depends on the message. A clear signal for December would back the hikes already priced and support the euro; a vague one, or worry about French borrowing at President Christine Lagarde's press conference, would leave it soft. The question to keep asking: does the ECB sound ready to keep raising rates while growth is slowing?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: euro-area economic sentiment at 5:00 AM CT, US growth and inflation figures at 7:30 AM CT, the ECB decision at 8:15 AM CT and Lagarde's press conference at about 8:45 AM CT. Euro-area growth and inflation estimates follow Friday.

ECB deposit rate 2.50%; October hold ~95% priced

scenarios.base: The ECB holds and keeps December open without a firm promise; the euro stays between about $1.110 and $1.120.
scenarios.bull: The ECB holds and clearly signals a December hike, and US inflation comes in soft; the euro rises above $1.120.
scenarios.bear: Lagarde sounds cautious on growth or is pressed on France, and US inflation runs hot; the euro falls below $1.110.

chapters.title: British Pound
chapters.teaser: The pound held near $1.333 overnight, steady after Chancellor John Healey's calm first Budget. Markets still expect the Bank of England to raise rates on November 5.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: UK inflation rose to 3.5% in September, and markets have priced a Bank of England hike on November 5 as almost certain. Healey's first Budget on Wednesday was the last big risk before that decision. What changed: Little overnight. The pound eased slightly to about $1.333 as the dollar steadied, after recovering from a 12-day low before the Budget speech. What it means: With the Budget out of the way and borrowing set to fall, the pound now moves mostly on the Bank of England and the US dollar. A near-certain UK hike already gives it support, so it needs a fresh surprise to move far. The question to keep asking: does anything shake the case for a November hike?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: UK money and credit figures at 4:30 AM CT, US growth and inflation figures at 7:30 AM CT, then the Bank of England decision on November 5 at 6:00 AM CT (US clocks change on November 1).

chapters.title: Japanese Yen
chapters.teaser: The dollar stayed just under ¥158, near ¥157.75. Japanese consumer confidence dipped slightly in October. Tokyo inflation figures come at 6:30 PM CT tonight, then the Bank of Japan decides overnight.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Japanese rates are far below US rates, which has kept the yen weak, and Tokyo has warned it is ready to act in the currency market. The Bank of Japan is expected to hold on Friday and raise rates in December. What changed: Overnight, Japan's consumer confidence index slipped to 35.0 from 35.4, just under forecasts, a sign households are a little more cautious. The dollar held near ¥157.75, below the ¥158 level it failed to keep after the Fed. What it means: A soft consumer reading does not change the December hike case on its own. Tokyo prices tonight are the last inflation check before the decision; firm prices would back a December hike and narrow the rate gap that keeps the yen weak. The question to keep asking: how soon does the Bank of Japan raise rates again?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: US growth and inflation figures at 7:30 AM CT, Tokyo consumer prices for October at 6:30 PM CT tonight (core forecast 2.6%), then the Bank of Japan decision and new forecasts during Friday in Japan (overnight Thursday CT).

chapters.title: Swiss Franc
chapters.teaser: The franc firmed slightly to about 0.828 per dollar overnight, with no Swiss news. It continues to move with global calm and fear rather than with Swiss data.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Swiss inflation is below target and the Swiss National Bank holds its rate at zero, so the franc mostly moves as a safe place for money in tense times. The bank has said it is less ready to fight a weaker franc. What changed: Little. The franc edged up to near 0.828 per dollar as the dollar eased against several currencies, while oil and Middle East tension both cooled a little. What it means: With no rate move in sight, the franc will keep following risk mood: a flare-up with Iran would lift it, steady calm would keep it soft. The question to keep asking: are investors looking for safety?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: Swiss National Bank board member Petra Tschudin speaks at 12:30 PM CT, and the KOF economic barometer comes at 3:00 AM CT Friday. The next Swiss rate decision is December 10.

scenarios.bear: Calm returns and US inflation runs hot; the dollar climbs above 0.835.

chapters.title: Australian Dollar
chapters.teaser: The Aussie held near 70.6 US cents, close to a five-week high. Australian import prices fell in the third quarter as oil shipping eased, but markets still expect a Reserve Bank of Australia hike on November 3.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Australian inflation has run above the Reserve Bank of Australia's forecasts, and the bank has raised rates four times this year. Hot third-quarter inflation figures on Wednesday made a fifth hike, on November 3, likely. What changed: Overnight, Australian import prices fell 1.1% in the third quarter, against a forecast rise, after a 5.7% jump in the second; cheaper fuel as shipping through the Strait of Hormuz reopened drove the drop. The Aussie barely moved, near 70.6 cents. What it means: Cheaper imports should ease price pressure later, but they do not undo the hot inflation the bank already has in hand, so the November hike case stands and keeps the Aussie supported. The question to keep asking: does anything talk the Reserve Bank of Australia out of November?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: US growth and inflation figures at 7:30 AM CT, Australian producer prices and private credit at 7:30 PM CT tonight, then the Reserve Bank of Australia decision at 9:30 PM CT Monday, November 2.

chapters.title: Canadian Dollar
chapters.teaser: The loonie strengthened to about 1.398 per US dollar overnight, building on the Bank of Canada's rate hike on Wednesday. Canada's August growth figures come Friday.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Higher energy prices pushed Canadian inflation up, and on Wednesday the Bank of Canada raised its rate to 2.50%, its first hike since 2023. Governor Tiff Macklem said more hikes are possible but the bank will proceed carefully. What changed: Overnight the loonie gained about 0.4%, moving from near 1.4035 to about 1.398 per US dollar, as the US dollar eased against commodity currencies. Markets give a second Canadian hike in December roughly even odds. What it means: Canada has joined the hiking camp, which narrows the rate gap with the US and supports the loonie, even with oil a little lower overnight. The question to keep asking: does Canadian data give the bank reason to hike again in December?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: US growth and inflation figures at 7:30 AM CT, Bank of Canada deputy governor Nicolas Vincent at 9:50 AM CT, then Canada's August GDP at 7:30 AM CT Friday. The next decision is December 9.

scenarios.bear: US inflation runs hot or oil slides further on Iran talks; the US dollar rises back above 1.405.

chapters.title: New Zealand Dollar
chapters.teaser: The kiwi recovered to about 56.25 US cents after Wednesday's drop on the central bank's surprise hold. A survey showed New Zealand business confidence edged up, and firms plan to raise prices more.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: On Wednesday the Reserve Bank of New Zealand held its rate at 2.75% in a 4–3 vote when almost everyone expected a hike, and the kiwi fell sharply. The bank said more tightening is likely. What changed: Overnight the ANZ business survey showed confidence rising to 52.5 from 51.9, and firms' pricing plans at their highest since May; their own activity outlook eased a little. Governor Anna Breman said the chance of a December hike is high. The kiwi edged up from about 56.06 to 56.25 cents. What it means: Firmer price plans strengthen the case for a December hike, so the hold looks like a delay rather than a change of mind, which limits the kiwi's downside. The question to keep asking: does the December hike look more certain?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: US growth and inflation figures at 7:30 AM CT. The next Reserve Bank of New Zealand decision is December 9, with new forecasts.
numbers: Firms' pricing intentions highest since May

chapters.title: Oil
chapters.teaser: Oil fell about 1%, with Brent near $114, after a report that US Vice President JD Vance wrote to a senior Iranian official to restart peace talks. Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia limited the drop.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: The US–Iran war, which began in February, disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and has kept oil above $100. Talk of renewed US strikes after next week's midterm elections had pushed prices back up this week. What changed: The Wall Street Journal reported that Vance wrote to Mohsen Rezaei, a senior Iranian security official, to explore restarting talks; President Donald Trump denied ordering talks. Brent fell about 1% to near $114 and US crude about 1.3% to near $101.5. Houthi claims of a strike on Saudi Arabia's largest refinery, still not confirmed by Saudi officials, kept prices from falling further. What it means: Oil is being pulled between hopes for a deal and fear of more fighting, so headlines move it more than supply data. A cheaper barrel helps importers like Japan and the euro area and takes a little support from exporters like Canada. The question to keep asking: are talks with Iran real enough to take the war premium out?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: any reply from Iran to the Vance letter, the OPEC+ meeting on Sunday, expected to keep December output targets unchanged, and the US midterm elections on Tuesday, November 3.
numbers: US crude stocks -1.9M barrels last week (EIA)

scenarios.bull: Iran rebuffs the letter or Saudi damage is confirmed; Brent climbs back above $118.
scenarios.bear: Iran agrees to formal talks; Brent falls below $110.

chapters.title: Gold
chapters.teaser: Gold fell about 0.7% to near $4,040 an ounce in Asia, as a likely December Fed hike and high yields weighed on it. It is on course for a second monthly fall.
chapters.meaning: The story so far: Gold soared earlier in the Iran war but has struggled since the Fed resumed raising rates, because higher yields make a metal that pays nothing less attractive. It is down about 2.5% in October. What changed: Overnight gold slipped to about $4,038, giving back Wednesday's small gain, as traders waited for US inflation figures. A Reuters poll showed analysts cutting their gold forecasts for a second straight quarter, citing high yields and a strong dollar. What it means: Gold is trading as a rates story: hot US inflation and a firmer December Fed hike would weigh on it, while soft data or a flare-up with Iran would help. The question to keep asking: are US real yields still rising?
chapters.fx: What's next: Coming up: US growth and PCE inflation figures at 7:30 AM CT and the ECB decision at 8:15 AM CT.

calls.text: Moody's review of France Fri: a downgrade widens France's gap over German yields and weighs on the euro; holding the rating eases the pressure
calls.note: Moody's held France at Aa3; French yields eased on Monday and the euro led the majors in the European morning.

calls.text: Bailey 8:00 AM CT after the 3.5% UK inflation print: backing November without promising more keeps the pound near $1.34; any opening to a December follow-up lifts it; calling energy temporary trims it
calls.note: Neither branch: Bailey gave no new signal on rates. The pound still held near $1.34 (about 1.3395 at the New York close), with December's second hike about a coin toss.

calls.text: US crude oil stocks 9:30 AM CT (industry survey: about −4.9M barrels): a big official draw keeps Brent above $110; a build lets the rebound fade
calls.note: The draw came (−3.1M barrels, far more than forecast) and Brent briefly topped $110.8, but it still faded to $108.82 at the settle after the US Treasury's tanker licence and emergency fuel loans.

calls.text: Pakistan's mediation after Iran's uranium refusal: any confirmed opening drains oil's premium and lifts the euro and yen; more warships and no talks keep Brent near $110 into the close
calls.note: No opening: Rubio called a deal extremely difficult and more US warships headed in. Brent settled at $108.82, near $110 but off its high on Washington's supply moves rather than diplomacy.

calls.text: Japan national CPI Thu 6:30 PM CT (2.1% expected): a hot print keeps the BoJ's December hike near three in four; a soft one fades it and weighs on the yen
calls.note: Neither branch: 2.1% exactly as expected (1.7% prior), though the measure that also leaves out energy jumped to 2.4%. December hike pricing held near 80%.

calls.text: US–Iran framework: confirmation by either government drains oil's risk premium and pulls US long yields lower; another denial puts Brent back toward $110
calls.note: No confirmation from either government, and no fresh denial either. Brent still climbed back toward $110 overnight, on tanker attacks spreading to the Gulf of Oman rather than on the talks.

calls.text: RBA's Hauser 5:30 PM CT: leaning on sticky inflation keeps a November hike near 1 in 3; leaning on the softer job market trims it
calls.note: Hauser leaned on sticky inflation: the outlook is 'materially worse'. Odds of a November hike rose to about 40% from about 30%, and the Aussie hit a three-week high near 0.702.

calls.text: China Q3 GDP 4.5% vs 4.4% fc — the aussie's demand read
calls.note: Beat: 4.5% vs 4.4% fc (q/q 1.2%); retail +1.1% the standout. AUD/USD +0.3-0.5% to ~0.697, the night's best G10 performer; USD/CNH 6.6811, strongest since June 2022. Two-speed beat (factories lead, property -20.6% YTD).

calls.text: Petersburg Oil Terminal drone strike — Baltic supply risk into Monday's open vs the waiver's lower-price pull
calls.note: Fire CONFIRMED (Beglov; Fire Point confirmed its FP-1 hit the terminal); ~1 killed, several injured (figures vary); damage extent still unquantified. Crude's Sunday open came flat — neither the spike nor the tumble; Asia Brent -1.0 to -1.8%.

calls.text: Beirut strike fallout: the haven-bid tell at Monday's open
calls.note: No Hezbollah retaliation as of Monday's open (Qmati: strike crossed a 'red line', leadership to decide; IDF: normal routines). Haven bid stayed sheathed — DXY flat 101.80-101.83, havens ~flat in Asia. The tell held: no escalation, no haven extension.

calls.text: October FOMC priced as a hold (~85%) into the Saturday blackout; December is the live debate
Brent broke $108 on Ukraine refinery strikes — $105-112 range into the weekend (prior $104-108 call broken)
USD/CAD holds 1.41-1.43 into the BoC (Oct 28); Canada CPI Mon the trigger
calls.note: Oct 19: CPI passed without a break — USD/CAD ~1.411 at the NY close, still inside the range. Runs to the Oct 28 decision. Oct 20: dipped to ~1.409, a hair under the floor, as oil and BoC hike bets lifted the loonie. Oct 20 close: broke below the floor — USD/CAD ~1.406, strongest loonie since Sep 22, on BoC hike pricing (~80–85%) and Alberta's vote to remain.
The tripwire never bit — Friday's waiver suspends the duties outright with no end date. Superseded by the ~Dec 17 60-day review clock.
calls.text: Graham Act Oct-18 tripwire: waivers extended or enforcement begins — oil's Sunday open is the tell
Iran deal Sunday signing: Trump's 'OPEN TO ALL' vs Tehran's 'not tomorrow' — the strait itself is the verdict
calls.note: No signed deal carried by any major wire by 4pm CT Sunday; Trump's 'complete' claim stands unverified against Tehran's 'talks stalled'. Aggregator 'markets celebrate' content held — its futures numbers contradict Friday's verified settles. The signing test is claim day, not done day.

calls.text: Canada CPI Mon 7:30am CT (TD 3.2%, UBS 3.3%, RBC 3.0%): hot (3.3%+) revives the Oct 28 hike; soft (3.0%-) buries it to December
calls.note: Neither branch: 3.1% vs 3.2% expected, core measures cooled to 1.8–1.9%. October stayed about 1 in 4 (a hold), with about one quarter-point hike priced by December; consumers' inflation expectations rose to ~3.9% in the BoC survey. Correction (Oct 20): by Monday's close swaps had jumped to ~87% for an October hike on Macklem's Saturday forecast warning; the 1-in-4 figure was stale.

calls.text: UK CPI Wed 1am CT (3.4% fc vs 3.1%): 3.5%+ starts pricing a December follow-up; soft reopens Bailey's 2027 read
calls.note: Hot branch: 3.5% vs 3.4% expected (3.1% in August), the highest in 11 months. November's hike is near certain; how much December moved was not yet verified at write.

calls.text: NZ Q3 CPI Wed 4:45pm CT (ANZ 3.8% y/y): hot settles the RBNZ's two-way bet toward the hike side
calls.note: Not hot: inflation came in at 3.7%, a touch soft. The hike side still settled anyway, with October 28 now about 98% priced.

calls.text: Japan CPI Fri + BoJ Oct 29-30: Ueda's 'quite close' language tested — October hike stays ~25%
calls.note: Oct 19: swaps now put an October 30 hike under 5% (BBH), below the ~25% in the call. December ~80% unchanged. October hike odds fell to about 4%, far below the ~25% in the call; Japan's inflation came in at 2.1% as expected and December (~80%) is now the meeting that matters.

calls.text: France's revenue-section budget vote Tue: a clean pass narrows the French–German spread (~141bp); a defeat or big concessions widens it and weighs on the euro
calls.note: No vote on Tuesday: it was pushed to October 27, so neither branch played out.

calls.text: UK jobs Tue 1 AM CT (earnings ~3.8% expected): sticky pay firms the BoE hike case before Wednesday's inflation; cooling pay backs Bailey's calmer view
calls.note: Sticky side won: unemployment fell to 4.7% (4.9% expected) and regular pay rose 3.7% (3.6% expected); total pay and claims were softer. Pound +0.3% to ~1.334.

calls.text: Konarak follow-through: a US confirmation or more strikes keeps oil's supply premium and lifts US yields; silence lets the morning's waiver drop resume
calls.note: No confirmation (a US official denied the strike) and no new strike overnight, yet the premium held: Brent ~$109.8 Tuesday on low Gulf flows and Iran's Hormuz claims. The waiver-driven drop did not resume.

calls.text: BoC Oct 28 with ~87% priced for a hike: a hike is mostly in the loonie already; a hold would be the surprise and hit it
NZ Q3 CPI Wed 4:45pm CT (~3.8% y/y): near forecast keeps the ~80% hike pricing; clearly soft reopens the hold and weighs on the kiwi
calls.note: Near forecast (3.7% vs 3.8%) and hike pricing held, rising to about 98%; the kiwi dipped only briefly.
